tendunt: tendō, tendere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, strain; to head for, make toward (3rd pl. pres.)
thybrim: Thybris, -idis (m.) — the Tiber (acc. sg., Greek form in -im)
troiae: Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (gen. sg.) · also dat. sg., for Troy (sīc fāta ferēbant)
troiana: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
tulit: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to bear, bring, carry; sē ferre, to betake oneself (3rd sg. perf.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turris: turris, -is (f.) — tower (acc. pl., = turrēs; also nom. sg./gen. sg.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
vectum: vehō, -ere, vexī, vectum — to carry; pass. to be borne, travel (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg.; also n. nom./acc. sg.)
vertere: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, change, drive (pres. inf.)
veterum: vetus, veteris — old, ancient, long-standing (gen. pl.)
virga: virga, -ae (f.) — twig, shoot, rod (nom. sg.; also abl. sg.)
vocavit: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon (3rd sg. perf.)
vox: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, sound (nom. sg.)
